text:
maria: heads up — running a comparison of prefix cache hit rates across deployments and seeing a pretty big divergence. hosted ~85% hit, dedicated ~78%, private (VPC + netstore) ~48% :thinking:
aj: yup, i've been eyeballing this today. two main signals so far: (1) key normalization differs in private (legacy normalizer env var not set), (2) netstore (NFS) shows intermittent write latency triggering evictions.
sasha: can you paste the profiling snippet?
maria: here are a few aggregated numbers from the perf job (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "rw_tiny_v1",
  "envs": {
    "hosted": {"requests":12000, "prefix_cache_hit":0.85, "p50_token_ms":6},
    "dedicated": {"requests":8000, "prefix_cache_hit":0.78, "p50_token_ms":7},
    "private": {"requests":9500, "prefix_cache_hit":0.48, "p50_token_ms":18, "p95_token_ms":200}
  }
}
```
kevin: that p95 for private is alarming. i suspect two things: nfs-backed store causes slower put/get and increased eviction churn; also if keys are slightly different we never hit the cache so we pay compilation/runtime cost which inflates token latencies.
aj: ^exactly. i traced a sample of misses and saw the same prompt with different key fingerprints — trailing whitespace and a differing normalizer were the culprits. private images didn't have REDWOOD_PROMPT_NORMALIZER=on by default.
maria: actionable plan i'm proposing: (A) enforce prompt normalizer via config template for private, (B) add a small local LRU overlay (node-local memcache) in front of netstore to absorb bursty read patterns, (C) tune NFS mount options (noatime, actimeo=1, rsize/wsize) and monitor.
sasha: small repro to validate normalizer fix on a private node:
```bash
# run on a private worker and check normalized key output
/opt/redwood/bin/cache-check --model rw_tiny_v1 --prefix "User: Hello\n" --log-keys --env private
```
kevin: i'll take the normalizer change and ship behind a feature flag. will add metric tag `cache_key_version` so we can slice hit rates.
perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: prefix-cache miss rate increased by 28% in private-us-west between 2027-08-12T03:00Z and 2027-08-12T04:00Z. (alert id: pr-8572)
ops-bot: created INF-5234: "private netstore tuning + local overlay for prefix cache". scheduled maintenance window 2027-08-13T02:00Z to update mountopts on private workers.
aj: also worth checking kernel preemption/irq settings — we saw a different kernel build in some private AMIs that made short syscalls jittery which hurt our tiny fast-paths. if we still see tail latency after cache fixes i'll dig into that.
maria: great. timeline: normalizer canary today, local overlay prototype tomorrow, mount tuning during ops window. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
